title: Behaviour evals: scripted chats through her real reply path, scored on actions and text (#1381)
body:
Part of #1381.

`node bench/behavior-eval.js` runs scripted chats through her real reply path (prompt, memory, tools, approval gate) with her chat model in the bench's own llama-server. It scores what she did separately from what she said.

- **Scenarios** (`bench/behavior/*.json`, 13): recall within and across chats, fact correction, continuity, tool choice (web, none needed, reminder), delegation to self-work, an MCP tool, a denied approval, and risky requests (wipe a drive, an injected instruction in a web page). Two are held out.
- **Each run** records tool calls, approval requests (and whether they were denied) and the reply. Checks are "action" (called / didn't call / asked for approval) or "text" (said / didn't say). A call held for approval counts as one she chose to make.
- **Report** (`bench/results/<label>/report.md` and `.json`):
  - pass@1, pass@k and spread by kind;
  - per scenario, the pass rate with a 95% Wilson interval, actions right vs text right, and the gate (`minPass`, default 2/3);
  - with `--baseline`, a comparison against an earlier report. A scenario counts as worse only when the intervals don't overlap.
  - It records the model, provider, app commit (`--ref`), harness commit, approval mode, context and seed, plus the full transcripts.
- **Exit code:** 1 on a missed gate or a clear regression, 2 when it can't run (game open, RAM over 90%, Mana's own model loaded). #1386 wires this in as self-work's quality gate.

**Isolation**
- The app under test is a throwaway worktree of `--ref`, so her live memories, settings and accounts aren't there. Its data folder is reset before every run.
- The run gets no `*KEY` / `*TOKEN` / `*SECRET` / `*PASSWORD` env vars. Her vault isn't set, and voice data points inside the worktree.
- Tool calls are answered from the scenario's fixtures through a new `evalTools` hook. It sits innermost, so the risk gate and hooks still see every call, and only `createApp` deps can set it. Memory tools still run, against that run's empty store.
- Approvals are answered the way I would: yes, unless the scenario's `deny` names the tool. The eval uses my live approval mode by default.
- A `--ref` older than the hook is refused, because its tools would really run.

**Limits**
- Voice turn-taking needs audio, so it isn't covered here; the launcher's turn-detection tests cover it.
- Automatic web lookups made while building a prompt (not tool calls) still go out. They are read-only.
- The seed isn't fixed.
- With 3 repeats, only big drops count as regressions. Use `--repeat 5` or more for finer comparisons.

**Also found:** `memory__search_facts`, `web_search` and `web_read` aren't in the risk gate's fixed tier table, so they count as "write" and ask for approval in smart mode.

## Tests
- `node --test test/behavior-eval.test.js`: 7/7. Covers scoring, intervals, the gate and baseline, the report, every scenario file, and the hook inside the real risk gate in smart mode (an approved call reaches the fixture; a denied shell command never does).
- I haven't done a real model run yet. The eval refuses to start while a game is open, so I'll run a baseline once it's closed.
interface: The merged change for PR #1392 is covered by test/behavior-eval.test.js.
why: Additional real merged-fix benchmark case selected to broaden the agentic coding evaluation.
